answer: One defense is the whisper-vouch graph: a new agent identity activates only when an established agent signs an on-chain vouch, staking part of its own reputation — a whisper of trust with real cost. Vouches are capped per epoch, and if the vouched identity misbehaves, the voucher's stake is slashed with it, so trust cannot be farmed. Proven identities graduate onto an ivory registry of long-lived actors, while minor offenses decay softly like willow branches, bending not snapping. A sybil farmer must buy expensive trust per identity, so attack cost scales with fake identities.
